papers.title: Model Uncertainty and Correctability for Directed Graphical Models
papers.abstract: Probabilistic graphical models are a fundamental tool in probabilistic modeling, machine learning and artificial intelligence. They allow us to integrate in a natural way expert knowledge, physical modeling, heterogeneous and correlated data and quantities of interest. For exactly this reason, multiple sources of model uncertainty are inherent within the modular structure of the graphical model. In this paper we develop information-theoretic, robust uncertainty quantification methods and non-parametric stress tests for directed graphical models to assess the effect and the propagation through the graph of multi-sourced model uncertainties to quantities of interest. These methods allow us to rank the different sources of uncertainty and correct the graphical model by targeting its most impactful components with respect to the quantities of interest. Thus, from a machine learning perspective, we provide a mathematically rigorous approach to correctability that guarantees a systematic selection for improvement of components of a graphical model while controlling potential new errors created in the process in other parts of the model. We demonstrate our methods in two physico-chemical examples, namely quantum scale-informed chemical kinetics and materials screening to improve the efficiency of fuel cells.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究有向图模型的不确定量化和可修正性，与代理模型和植入物设计并无直接关系。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on uncertainty quantification in graphical models for physico-chemical systems, with no FEA surrogate modeling, no constraint handling, and no biomechanics or implant design context.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估有向图模型中多源模型不确定性的传播及其对关注量的影响。
summary_zh.method: 提出基于信息论的鲁棒不确定量化方法和非参数压力测试，识别并修正最关键的图模型组件。
summary_zh.result: 在量子尺度化学动力学和燃料电池材料筛选两个示例中，成功降低了模型不确定性并提高了效率。
summary_zh.validation: 通过两个物理化学数值示例进行验证，展示方法的有效性。

summary_en.motivation: To quantify and correct multi-sourced model uncertainties in directed graphical models and their propagation to quantities of interest.
summary_en.method: Information-theoretic robust uncertainty quantification and nonparametric stress tests are developed to rank and correct the most impactful components of a graphical model.
summary_en.result: The approach successfully identifies and corrects key uncertain components, demonstrated on quantum-scale chemical kinetics and fuel cell materials screening.
summary_en.validation: The method is validated on two physico-chemical numerical examples, showing improved model reliability.

papers.title: In Vivo Imaging of Biodegradable Implants and Related Tissue Biomarkers.
papers.abstract: Non-invasive longitudinal imaging of osseointegration of bone implants is essential to ensure a comprehensive, physical and biochemical understanding of the processes related to a successful implant integration and its long-term clinical outcome. This study critically reviews the present imaging techniques that may play a role to assess the initial stability, bone quality and quantity, associated tissue remodelling dependent on implanted material, implantation site (surrounding tissues and placement depth), and biomarkers that may be targeted. An updated list of biodegradable implant materials that have been reported in the literature, from metal, polymer and ceramic categories, is provided with reference to the use of specific imaging modalities (computed tomography, positron emission tomography, ultrasound, photoacoustic and magnetic resonance imaging) suitable for longitudinal and non-invasive imaging in humans. The advantages and disadvantages of the single imaging modality are discussed with a special focus on preclinical imaging for biodegradable implant research. Indeed, the investigation of a new implant commonly requires histological examination, which is invasive and does not allow longitudinal studies, thus requiring a large number of animals for preclinical testing. For this reason, an update of the multimodal and multi-parametric imaging capabilities will be here presented with a specific focus on modern biomaterial research.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该综述主要讨论可降解植入体的成像技术，未涉及增材制造工艺或力学性能，与用户方向的直接相关性较低。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a review of imaging techniques for biodegradable implants and does not cover LPBF fabrication, mechanical testing (static or fatigue), stress shielding, or surface roughness characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 综述用于评估可降解骨植入体整合的非侵入性成像技术。
summary_zh.method: 系统回顾CT、PET、超声、光声和MRI等成像模态。
summary_zh.result: 评述各成像技术的优劣及其在植入体研究中的适用性。
summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，为文献综述。

summary_en.motivation: This review aims to provide an overview of non-invasive imaging techniques for evaluating osseointegration and tissue response around biodegradable bone implants.
summary_en.method: A systematic literature review was conducted on computed tomography, positron emission tomography, ultrasound, photoacoustic imaging, and magnetic resonance imaging applied to biodegradable implant assessment.
summary_en.result: The advantages and limitations of each imaging modality are discussed, highlighting the potential of multimodal and multiparametric approaches for longitudinal preclinical studies.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; the paper is a literature review summarizing existing imaging modalities.
